truncation.hint: The engine returned a page of the roster, not every tenant. The total CANNOT be inferred from the loaded rows — a tenant that is not listed here may still exist, and may still be served.

title: Tenants
description: Withdraw or restore a tenant's service — that part is lossless. Deleting a tenant is a separate, permanent action.
emptyHint: The system roster is empty, or this deployment has a single tenant.
unknownHint: The engine reported a service state this console does not know. It is shown as-is rather than assumed active.
suspendDescription: Mutations and interactive service are refused with 423 tenant_suspended until service is restored.
keepsAuth: Authentication and the operator's system routes, so the tenant can be explained and restored.
keepsExport: Export of the tenant's own data — withdrawing service must not hold a customer's data hostage. An export taken while service is withdrawn is recorded on the tenant's own audit chain.
keepsCustody: Custodial work: the chain keeps being checkpointed and stays verifiable and backup-certifiable.
notDelete: This does not delete anything. Deleting a tenant is a separate, destructive operation.
restoreDescription: Service is restored losslessly: nothing was deleted while it was withdrawn.
deleteDescription: This purges the tenant and its data immediately. It cannot be undone and there is no recovery window in this engine.
deleteGrace: The 30-day grace period documented for the API belongs to the cloud control plane, not to this engine. Here the purge happens the moment you confirm.
deleteInstead: To stop serving a customer without destroying anything, suspend instead — suspending is lossless and reversible.
deleteSystem: The system tenant cannot be deleted
